stem: A developer marks a subsection with `<h4>` because the text should look smaller than the page's `<h2>` sections. What is the accessibility problem?

options.text: Heading levels should follow structure, not visual size.
options.rationale: Screen reader users navigate by heading level, so a level chosen for appearance misrepresents the page's structure.

options.text: A page may use a single heading level throughout its content.
options.rationale: Pages normally use several heading levels to express hierarchy; using one level throughout would remove that structure.

options.text: `<h4>` is reserved for footers and sidebars.
options.rationale: Heading levels are not reserved for particular page regions; they describe the depth of the content.

options.text: Headings should include visible numbers in their text.
options.rationale: Visible numbers are optional; the heading level itself provides the structure for assistive technology.

explanation: Screen reader users navigate by heading levels, so a skipped level suggests missing structure. Choose the heading level that matches the content hierarchy and use CSS to change its visual size.
